name: AES Corporation
description: AES owns and operates power plants and regulated utilities around the world. Its Renewables unit builds and runs solar, wind, storage and hydro under long-term contracts (increasingly with data-center companies; backlog of signed projects 12.0 GW, 5.7 GW under construction); its Utilities unit (AES Indiana, AES Ohio and four utilities in El Salvador) distributes power to 2.7 million customers on regulated returns; Energy Infrastructure runs gas, LNG, coal and other plants. On March 1, 2026 AES agreed to be bought for $15.00 a share in cash by funds managed by Global Infrastructure Management and EQT Infrastructure VI; shareholders approved on June 26, 2026 and closing is expected late 2026 or early 2027, subject to regulators. The Renewables and Energy Infrastructure generation units supply about 71% of segment Adjusted EBITDA and the regulated Utilities unit about 30% (computed), so the Independent Power Producer label fits only part of it.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Utilities' and Sub-Industry 'Independent Power Producers & Energy Traders' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 4991 (Cogeneration Services & Small Power Producers) per EDGAR.

employees.note: Full-time/permanent employees; about 31% of US employees under collective bargaining agreements and about 48% of the non-US workforce (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Renewables SBU
businessLines.how: Sells electricity (and renewable certificates) under long-term power purchase agreements, where the energy price on the entire output is set by the contract, plus US tax credits that AES monetises ($1.5B of tax attributes recognised in 2025); profit comes from plant output and contract price, so growth depends on building the backlog.
businessLines.description: Solar, wind, energy storage and hydro generation facilities, selling power under long-term contracts to utilities, corporations and data-center customers.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP; the measure the company uses to run its SBUs); operating margin $503M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874761/000087476126000063/aes-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: Utilities SBU
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated rates monthly; the US utilities earn an allowed return on rate base set by state regulators (IURC in Indiana; PUCO approval is also needed for the merger because of AES Ohio) and pass through fuel and purchased power; El Salvador utilities earn regulated distribution tariffs.
businessLines.description: AES Indiana (integrated), AES Ohio (transmission and distribution) and four AES utilities in El Salvador: 2.7 million customers and 4,056 MW of US generation.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP; the measure the company uses to run its SBUs); operating margin $635M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874761/000087476126000063/aes-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: Energy Infrastructure SBU
businessLines.how: Sells electricity from gas, LNG, coal and other plants under medium and long-term contracts, where the 10-K says there is limited price competition during the term, and into short-term markets, where dispatch and price are set by market competition.
businessLines.description: Natural gas, LNG, coal, pet coke, diesel and oil generation facilities.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP; the measure the company uses to run its SBUs); operating margin $901M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874761/000087476126000063/aes-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: New Energy Technologies SBU
businessLines.how: Equity stakes and development spending rather than revenue; the segment lost money (Adjusted EBITDA -$35M in 2025).
businessLines.description: Investments in Fluence, Maximo and other new energy technology businesses (minority and early-stage holdings); Uplight stake being sold.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP; the measure the company uses to run its SBUs); operating margin $-11M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874761/000087476126000063/aes-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: Corporate and other; eliminations
businessLines.description: Corporate revenue and eliminations of intersegment sales.

operatingProfit.note: Corporate and other -$29M plus eliminations $10M in the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (computed; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874761/000087476126000063/aes-20251231.htm)

brands.name: AES Indiana, AES Ohio, AES El Salvador utilities
brands.note: 2.7 million customers across the six utilities; customers per utility not extracted

brands.name: AES Clean Energy
brands.note: US renewables development arm named in the 10-K; revenue not separately disclosed

brands.name: Fluence and Maximo
brands.note: Investments in Fluence Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FLNC; previously a joint venture with Siemens) and Maximo; revenue not consolidated

whatsNext.text: Merger with Horizon Parent, L.P. (funds managed by Global Infrastructure Management and EQT Infrastructure VI) at $15.00 cash per share: signed Mar 1, 2026, stockholders approved Jun 26, 2026, expected to close late 2026 or early 2027 pending PUCO, New York PSC, FERC and CFIUS approvals; outside date Jun 1, 2027 (extendable by two three-month periods); termination fees $100M or about $588M payable by the buyer, about $321M payable by AES in specified cases
Sale of 25% Uplight interest and convertible note for up to $40M, expected to close in the second half of 2026
